question: What is the primary underlying cause of inherited degenerative diseases?
explanation: These conditions stem directly from inherited alterations in DNA that lead to progressive cellular deterioration. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h1)

question: Why can diagnosing inherited degenerative diseases be particularly challenging in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Genetic mutations only manifest in individuals over the age of eighty
options.B: Laboratory tests can definitively cure the condition within days
options.C: Symptoms frequently overlap with common chronic infectious and nutritional disorders
options.D: Patients rarely present with any noticeable physical symptoms early on

explanation: Shared clinical presentations like weakness and gait changes can mimic more prevalent regional pathologies, delaying specific genetic recognition. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h1)

question: Which cellular abnormality involves the abnormal clumping of mutated proteins?
explanation: Mutant proteins fail to fold correctly and accumulate into toxic clumps that disrupt cellular machinery. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h2)

question: How does excitotoxicity directly damage neurons in degenerative conditions?

options.A: By inducing rapid replication of glial scar tissue
options.B: By completely blocking the production of cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: By depleting all available glucose stores in the bloodstream instantly
options.D: By causing a destructive influx of calcium ions via excessive glutamate activity

explanation: Overactivation of receptors by neurotransmitters like glutamate lets damaging levels of calcium flood the intracellular space. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h2)

question: Which feature is most characteristic of the earliest stages of inherited degenerative diseases?

options.A: Sudden and complete loss of consciousness
options.D: Subtle and easily overlooked functional declines

explanation: Early symptoms start mildly and develop gradually, often blending into normal daily fatigue or minor aches. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h3)

question: Why do healthcare providers frequently miss the earliest manifestations of these disorders?

options.A: Diagnostic guidelines strictly prohibit evaluation before age sixty
options.B: Blood tests always show completely normal values for the first decade
options.C: The initial signs mimic ordinary fatigue or normal aging processes
options.D: Patients refuse to visit a clinic until they are completely bedridden

explanation: Minor clumsiness or slight stamina drops are easily attributed to stress or everyday tiredness rather than a progressive genetic illness. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is a primary clinical sign of upper motor neuron involvement in degenerative conditions?

options.C: Complete absence of deep tendon reflexes

explanation: Upper motor neuron damage typically results in increased muscle tone and exaggerated reflex responses. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h4)

question: A patient with an inherited degenerative disorder presents with involuntary, rapid, irregular dance-like movements of the limbs. Which structure is most likely undergoing degeneration?
explanation: Chorea and involuntary movement disorders are classic hallmarks of basal ganglia dysfunction. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h4)

question: Which symptom category includes impairments in planning, abstract thinking, and organization?
explanation: Higher-level cognitive processes governed by the frontal lobes are collectively termed executive functions. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h5)

question: Why is obtaining a history from a family caregiver essential when evaluating cognitive decline?

options.A: Caregivers are legally required to sign all nursing care plans
options.B: Patients completely lose the ability to speak any language
options.C: Caregivers perform the formal neurological physical examination
options.D: Patients often lack insight into their own subtle behavioral and memory changes

explanation: Anosognosia or simple memory fading prevents patients from accurately reporting their own cognitive slips. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h5)

question: Which complication is a direct result of autonomic nervous system failure in degenerative diseases?
explanation: Autonomic dysfunction impairs blood pressure regulation upon standing, causing sudden drops and dizziness. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the primary danger associated with loss of proprioception in degenerative disorders?

options.A: Complete inability to perceive bright lights in dark rooms
options.B: Permanent paralysis of the facial muscles
options.C: Sudden loss of the sense of taste and smell
options.D: Increased risk of falls due to impaired spatial awareness of limb position

explanation: Without unconscious feedback regarding joint and muscle position, maintaining upright balance becomes exceptionally difficult. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is a major cause of mortality in the advanced stages of degenerative neurological diseases?
explanation: Progressive dysphagia leads to food and secretions entering the airway, frequently sparking fatal pulmonary infections. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h7)

question: Which nursing intervention is most critical for a bedridden patient in the final stage of a degenerative illness?

options.A: Restricting all family visits to prevent emotional overstimulation
options.B: Regular repositioning and meticulous skin care to prevent pressure ulcers
options.C: Administering large oral meals three times daily without assistance
options.D: Encouraging high-intensity marathon training to rebuild muscle mass

explanation: Immobility combined with tissue wasting makes skin breakdown an imminent and dangerous threat. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of utilizing validated rating scales during patient assessment?

options.A: To accurately track longitudinal disease progression and functional decline
options.B: To eliminate the need for any physical neurological examinations
options.C: To determine the exact date of patient discharge from the hospital
options.D: To instantly cure the underlying genetic mutation causing the illness

explanation: Standardized scales provide objective metrics to measure how symptoms change over weeks, months, and years. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard focus area during comprehensive nursing assessment for degenerative diseases?

options.A: Complete genetic sequencing of distant family members

explanation: Sequencing distant relatives is a specialized diagnostic genetic task, whereas nurses focus on clinical symptom management, nutrition, respiration, and caregiver support. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h8)
